title: End of the page: freeze the fading section's shimmer, on top of the GPU-morph build (rev 3)
problem:
Rev 3 is built on the GPU-morph build (PR-030), as you asked. It only makes sense if you accept PR-030.

Your notes, point by point:

1. Rev 1: "(b) has a bug: the background fades out sometimes at Serious."
- (b) is gone. (a) does not touch how the section fades: blur and transparency are exactly the GPU-morph build's.
- iPhone check at Serious: the fade measured the same at all 5 positions in both builds. Slow frames were no worse (table below).
- So whatever you see in A's fade, B shows the same. Please look at the fade in Try-it on the phone.

2. Rev 1: "try the arch-compositor-morph experiment instead." Done: it is PR-030, and this revision sits on top of it.

3. Rev 2: "Waiting for arch-compositor-morph done." It is done (PR-030). (a) applies to it without a single edit.

Background:
- At the end of the page the big end panel grows over the last section (the four feature rows).
- Over the first 55 % of that growth the section fades out: blurrier and more transparent, until it is invisible.
- Meanwhile 4 endless shimmers keep running in it (iPhone count): colour sweeps over the row titles and glints.
- Pausing them once the section is fully invisible needs no decision: it is already in the next build.
idea:
(a) freezes the section's shimmers from the first moment of the fade.
- They stop where they are when the fade starts.
- The blur and the fade stay exactly as in the GPU-morph build.
- Scroll back up and they continue from where they stopped.

In Try-it, A is the GPU-morph build (PR-030) and B is the GPU-morph build plus (a).
looksSame:
The blur, the fade, the panel and every colour are unchanged.
- Only the shimmers stop moving while the section fades.
- Most of that time the section is already blurred and half transparent.
visualDiff:
Still frames in Chrome: no difference, 0 px² at all 18 positions.
- Phone size (430x775), through the whole end morph, compared like for like.
- Your pixel rule (PR-010) allows at most 0.5 % of the screen.

Still frames in the iPhone Simulator: at most 83 px² (0.02 % of the screen), far under the 0.5 % limit.
- 83 px² before the morph starts, where (a) does nothing yet: Simulator noise.
- 13 px² in the nav logo, which (a) never touches, the same Simulator noise as before.
The change is in motion only: the shimmers stop moving during the fade. A still-frame check can't see that, so please judge it in Try-it.

gain.how: iPhone 15 Pro Max at Serious, counted at 5 positions of the fade, one check per build. Not a timing test.

gain.what: Slow frames over 50 ms in 2 morph runs (iPhone)
gain.how: iPhone at Serious, scripted open and close of the end panel, 3 cycles per run, order A B B A. Too few runs to call a gain.

gain.what: Slow frames over 34 ms in the same runs

risk:
The gain is small and unproven in time: the iPhone frames are the same within run-to-run variation.
- It depends on PR-030: if you decline PR-030, decline this too.
- The frozen shimmer is a visible change, small and only during the fade.

shots.caption: Fade half done (430x775), still frame: identical. The change is motion only (shimmers stop).
